svg.title: What a standards-compliant trace records by default, and what you have to switch on
svg.desc: Two panels side by side. The left panel lists what an OpenTelemetry instrumentation records without being asked: the operation name, the requested and responding model, input and output token totals, finish reasons, the conversation identifier and compaction flag, the tool name and tool call identifier, the trace, span and parent span identifiers, span start and end times, and the error type. The right panel, highlighted, lists what the standard marks Opt-In or does not define at all: the tool call arguments and result, the input and output messages, tool-result tokens per result, the number of tool results in one reply, the pass index, the run stop reason, and the retrieved document identifiers. A footer states that the dividing line is who has to act: four of the right-hand fields exist and are switched off because the standard warns they may hold sensitive information, and the rest have no attribute at all.

svg.text: The line between the panels is not importance. It is who has to act. Four fields on the right exist in the standard

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: and are switched off, because it warns each of them may contain sensitive information. The rest have no attribute

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: at all: the conventions do not model an agent's per-pass accounting, so those fields are ones you name yourself.
